learning_activity_name: Utiliser des accents et des intonations appropriés dans des conversations
sla_assessment_criteria: Capacité d’utiliser des accents et des intonations correctement.
sla_teaching_aids: Des textes audio visuel des accents et intonation française|Carte de sons
sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D’ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ire À IVe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: French uses written accents and a rising or falling melody to signal meaning and mood. Learners practise hearing and reproducing them in short conversations.
sla_notes_details: French has five accents: the acute (é) gives the closed sound /e/ as in été; the grave (è, à, ù) gives the open sound /ɛ/ as in père, and distinguishes words such as a and à or ou and où; the circumflex (ê, â, ô, î, û) often marks a lost letter as in forêt; the cedilla (ç) makes c soft before a, o, u as in garçon; the diaeresis (ë, ï) shows that two vowels are pronounced separately as in Noël. Intonation rises at the end of a yes/no question (Tu viens ?), falls at the end of a statement (Je viens.) and falls after a question word (Où vas-tu ?). Stress in French falls on the last pronounced syllable of a group of words.
sla_notes_illustrations: The teacher reads Tu habites à Dodoma ? with rising intonation and Oui, j'habite à Dodoma. with falling intonation. Pupils repeat, then pair up and act a short dialogue at a bus stop, marking accents and arrows for intonation on the script.
sla_notes_daily_life: Correct accents and intonation help you be understood when you greet a French-speaking visitor, order food in a restaurant, or work in tourism where French speakers are common.
sla_exercise: Which accent is on the letter e in été?::The acute accent, giving the closed sound /e/.||How does the voice move at the end of the question Tu viens ?::It rises.||Add the missing accents: ou est la ecole?::Où est l'école ?

sla_notes_intro: Punctuation organises written French and shows where to pause, ask or exclaim. Pupils learn to recognise and use the main marks correctly.
sla_notes_details: The main marks are the point (.) ending a statement, the virgule (,) separating items or clauses, the point d'interrogation (?), the point d'exclamation (!), the deux-points (:) introducing a list or speech, the point-virgule (;), the points de suspension (...), the guillemets (« ») used for speech, the tiret (-) for dialogue and hyphenated words, and the apostrophe (') for elision as in l'ami. French places a space before ? ! : and ; and inside guillemets. A sentence begins with a capital letter, but days, months and languages are written in lower case: lundi, mars, le français.
sla_notes_illustrations: Punctuate: bonjour comment allez vous. Answer: Bonjour, comment allez-vous ? Pupils then hunt for each mark in a short printed dialogue and name its role.
sla_notes_daily_life: Well-punctuated messages, emails and posters are clear to readers; a missing comma or question mark can change the meaning of a text message or a notice.
sla_exercise: Which mark introduces a list in French?::The deux-points (:).||Punctuate: Quelle heure est-il::Quelle heure est-il ?||Write the French word for the mark used in l'ami.::L'apostrophe.

sla_assessment_criteria: Capacité d’utiliser le dictionnaire.
sla_teaching_aids: Des textes écrits pour trouver les sens de mots
sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D’ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ire À IVe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: A dictionary is the learner's main tool for discovering new words independently. Pupils learn how entries are arranged and how to read them.
sla_notes_details: Words are listed alphabetically. Each entry gives the headword, its abbreviation for grammatical class (n.m. nom masculin, n.f. nom féminin, v. verbe, adj. adjectif, adv. adverbe), pronunciation in phonetic symbols, one or more meanings and an example sentence. In a bilingual dictionary, the learner reads both the French–English or French–Swahili section and the reverse section. Steps: find the first letter, then the second and third letters, read all senses, choose the one that fits the context, and note the gender of nouns (le, la). For verbs the dictionary lists the infinitive, so conjugated forms such as mangeons must be traced back to manger.
sla_notes_illustrations: To find the meaning of cahier, the pupil opens to C, then ca-, and finds cahier n.m. exercise book. The pupil writes: J'écris dans mon cahier.
sla_notes_daily_life: Using a dictionary helps you read French labels, instructions and websites and learn new words even when the teacher is absent.
sla_exercise: How is the noun école marked for gender in a dictionary?::n.f. (nom féminin).||Which infinitive should you look up for nous mangeons?::Manger.||Why should you read the example sentence in an entry?::It shows how the word is used in context.

sla_notes_intro: Vocabulary about familiar contexts such as school, family, food and the home lets pupils express themselves. Pupils use it in speech and writing.
sla_notes_details: Basic thematic vocabulary includes greetings (bonjour, salut, au revoir), family (le père, la mère, le frère, la soeur), school objects (le stylo, la règle, le cahier, le livre), colours, numbers 0 to 100, days and months, food (le pain, l'eau, le riz) and places (la maison, l'école, le marché). Nouns take a gender and an article: le or la (definite), un or une (indefinite), les or des (plural). Adjectives agree in gender and number: un grand livre, une grande table. Pupils use vocabulary through descriptions, guessing games and labelling.
sla_notes_illustrations: Describe an object: C'est un stylo. Il est bleu. Il est sur la table. In a guessing game one pupil says: C'est rouge, on écrit avec, and the class answers: un stylo rouge.
sla_notes_daily_life: Everyday vocabulary lets you introduce yourself, describe your home and shop when speaking with French-speaking neighbours or tourists.
sla_exercise: Give the definite article for the noun école.::La.||Translate: my brother.::Mon frère.||Complete: Une table ___ (grand).::Une grande table.

sla_notes_intro: Simple tenses let pupils talk about what is happening now, what happened and what will happen. Pupils identify them in texts and use them in sentences.
sla_notes_details: The present tense of regular -er verbs takes the endings -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent: je parle, tu parles, il parle, nous parlons, vous parlez, ils parlent. Être (je suis, tu es, il est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils sont) and avoir (j'ai, tu as, il a, nous avons, vous avez, ils ont) are irregular and essential. The near future is formed with aller plus the infinitive: Je vais manger. The passé composé uses avoir or être plus the past participle: J'ai mangé. The negative is formed with ne ... pas around the verb: Je ne parle pas.
sla_notes_illustrations: Text: Le matin, Amina se lève, elle mange du pain et va à l'école. Pupils underline present-tense verbs (se lève, mange, va) and rewrite the text in the near future: Amina va se lever, elle va manger.
sla_notes_daily_life: Talking about daily routines, plans for the weekend and past events is part of every conversation in any language.
sla_exercise: Conjugate parler with nous.::Nous parlons.||Write in the negative: Il mange.::Il ne mange pas.||Change to near future: Je regarde la télé.::Je vais regarder la télé.

sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D’ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ire À IVe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Pupils listen to a short audio or spoken text and pass on the main information in their own words.
sla_notes_details: Effective listening has three steps: before listening, predict from the title or context; while listening, note key words such as who, what, where, when; after listening, reconstruct the message. Reporting uses verbs such as dire, annoncer, expliquer and phrases like Il dit que ..., Selon le message ..., On annonce que .... Questions to guide understanding are Qui parle ?, De quoi parle-t-on ?, Où ?, Quand ?. Pupils should keep the order of the events and avoid adding invented details.
sla_notes_illustrations: After hearing a radio announcement: Le marché ouvre à huit heures samedi, a pupil reports: On annonce que le marché ouvre samedi à huit heures. Another pupil states who announced it and when.
sla_notes_daily_life: Understanding and repeating announcements at school, on the radio and in public places allows you to follow instructions accurately.
sla_exercise: Which question word asks about the place?::Où.||Give a phrase to start reporting a message.::Il dit que ... or On annonce que ....||Why should you note key words while listening?::They help you remember the main information to report.

sla_notes_intro: Pupils read short written texts and report their content orally or in writing.
sla_notes_details: Reading strategies include looking at the title and layout, skimming for the general idea, scanning for specific facts (names, dates, places), and rereading difficult sentences. To report, the pupil identifies the who, what, where, when and why, then rephrases using own words and reporting verbs. Texts at this level include notices, short letters, advertisements and messages. Note that, when reporting, first-person forms change to third person: Je viens demain becomes Il dit qu'il vient demain.
sla_notes_illustrations: Notice: La bibliothèque est fermée lundi. Report: Selon l'affiche, la bibliothèque ne sera pas ouverte lundi. Pupils discuss in groups what the notice means for them.
sla_notes_daily_life: Reading and reporting notices, messages and instructions helps you at school, at work and when travelling.
sla_exercise: What does scanning mean?::Reading quickly to find specific information such as a date or a name.||Report: Elle dit: Je viens demain.::Elle dit qu'elle vient demain.||Name two kinds of short written text.::A notice and a short letter (also an advertisement).

sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D’ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ire À IVe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Fluent reading means reading aloud and silently at a natural pace with correct pronunciation and understanding.
sla_notes_details: Fluency depends on accurate sound-letter correspondence: ou is /u/, ai is /ɛ/, eau is /o/, ch is /ʃ/, gn is /ɲ/, the final consonant is generally silent (petit, grand), and liaison links a final silent consonant to the next vowel (les amis /lezami/). Pupils practise reading in groups of words, respecting punctuation, and rereading a text several times. Silent letters and elision (l'école, j'aime) should be recognised. Pace should not be so fast that meaning is lost.
sla_notes_illustrations: The teacher reads Les enfants jouent dans la cour. Pupils read after her, linking les enfants and stopping at the full stop. Then pupils read in pairs and correct each other.
sla_notes_daily_life: Reading fluently allows you to read signs, menus, instructions and stories in French without hesitation.
sla_exercise: How is eau pronounced?::/o/.||What is a liaison?::Pronouncing a normally silent final consonant before a following vowel, as in les amis.||Which mark tells the reader to pause at the end of a sentence?::The full stop (point).

sla_assessment_criteria: Capacité de présenter des informations.
sla_teaching_aids: Des textes authentiques|Audio visuels des sujets differents
sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D’ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ire À IVe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Pupils role-play situations in which they ask for and give personal and practical information on familiar topics.
sla_notes_details: Questions can be formed by intonation (Tu vas bien ?), with est-ce que (Est-ce que tu habites ici ?) or by inversion (Habites-tu ici ?). Question words include qui, que, où, quand, comment, pourquoi, combien. Useful expressions: Pouvez-vous m'aider ?, Excusez-moi, Je voudrais ..., Merci beaucoup, De rien. For subjects such as health, travel or a meeting, learners use vocabulary like J'ai mal à la tête, Je vais chez le médecin, Le train part à dix heures. Politeness uses vous with strangers and tu with friends.
sla_notes_illustrations: Role-play at a health centre: Bonjour docteur, j'ai mal à la tête depuis hier. Doctor: Avez-vous de la fièvre ? Patient: Non, mais je suis fatigué. Pupils swap roles.
sla_notes_daily_life: Asking for directions, prices and help in French is useful when meeting French-speaking visitors or travelling in French-speaking countries.
sla_exercise: Turn into a question with est-ce que: Tu habites ici.::Est-ce que tu habites ici ?||Which pronoun is used with a stranger, tu or vous?::Vous.||Translate: I would like a glass of water.::Je voudrais un verre d'eau.

sla_assessment_criteria: Capacité de communiquer par lettre amicale.

sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D’ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ire À IVe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Pupils learn to write short, clear texts such as friendly letters and messages on familiar subjects.
sla_notes_details: A friendly letter has the place and date at the top right (Dodoma, le 5 mars 2024), a greeting (Cher Paul, Chère Marie), an introduction (Comment vas-tu ?), a body with news or questions, a closing sentence (J'espère te voir bientôt), a leave-taking formula (Amitiés, À bientôt, Je t'embrasse) and the signature. Paragraphs are short, sentences begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop. Use simple present and passé composé forms and connectors like et, mais, alors, parce que.
sla_notes_illustrations: Model: Cher Paul, Comment vas-tu ? Moi, je vais bien. J'étudie à l'école secondaire de Dodoma. Et toi ? Écris-moi bientôt. Amitiés, Neema. Pupils write a similar letter to a friend.
sla_notes_daily_life: Writing personal messages, invitations and short emails lets you keep in touch with friends and correspondents abroad.
sla_exercise: Where is the date written in a friendly letter?::At the top right of the page.||Give a closing formula for a friendly letter.::Amitiés, À bientôt or Je t'embrasse.||Which connector means because?::Parce que.

sla_notes_intro: Building on Form I, pupils widen their vocabulary on themes such as health, travel, the market and leisure and use it accurately.
sla_notes_details: New word fields include the body (la tête, le bras, la jambe), clothes (la robe, la chemise), transport (le bus, le train, l'avion), professions (le médecin, l'enseignant, le fermier) and the town (la poste, la banque, l'hôpital). Word families help: travailler, le travail, le travailleur. Prepositions of place are added: sur, sous, devant, derrière, à côté de, entre. Partitive articles express quantity: du pain, de la viande, de l'eau, des fruits, and after a negative or a quantity expression become de: Je n'ai pas de pain, beaucoup de fruits.
sla_notes_illustrations: Pupils describe a picture of a market: Il y a beaucoup de fruits sur la table. La vendeuse est derrière le comptoir. Je voudrais un kilo de tomates.
sla_notes_daily_life: A wider vocabulary lets you shop, describe places and talk about jobs and health in real conversations.
sla_exercise: Give the partitive article for eau.::De l'eau.||Translate: behind the school.::Derrière l'école.||Complete: Je n'ai pas ___ pain.::de

sla_notes_intro: Pupils combine vocabulary and grammar rules to write connected paragraphs.
sla_notes_details: A good paragraph has a topic sentence, supporting sentences and a conclusion, linked by connectors: d'abord, ensuite, puis, enfin, mais, car, donc. Grammar to control includes agreement of adjectives (une petite fille), possessives (mon, ma, mes, ton, ta, tes, son, sa, ses), the passé composé with avoir (J'ai fini) and with être for verbs of movement (Elle est allée), and the use of pronouns (il, elle, ils, elles) to avoid repetition. Pupils draft, check agreement and spelling, and rewrite.
sla_notes_illustrations: Sample: Samedi dernier, je suis allé au marché avec ma mère. D'abord, nous avons acheté des légumes. Ensuite, nous avons pris le bus. Enfin, nous sommes rentrés à la maison.
sla_notes_daily_life: Writing correct paragraphs prepares you for reports, emails and application letters.
sla_exercise: Give the auxiliary for aller in the passé composé.::Être.||Which connector means finally?::Enfin.||Put in the plural: la petite fille.::Les petites filles.

sla_assessment_criteria: Capacité d’écouter et résumer des messages dans des textes.

sla_notes_intro: Pupils listen to varied texts and summarise the essential points.
sla_notes_details: To summarise, note key words while listening, group related ideas, delete examples and details, and rewrite in about one third of the length using own words. A summary answers Qui ? Quoi ? Où ? Quand ? Pourquoi ?. Useful expressions are Le texte parle de ..., L'auteur explique que ..., En résumé, .... A summary keeps the order of ideas and gives no personal opinion.
sla_notes_illustrations: After hearing a five-line news item on a school festival, pupils write: Le texte parle d'une fête à l'école samedi. Les élèves présentent des chansons. Les parents sont invités.
sla_notes_daily_life: Summarising lets you report the content of a lecture, a meeting or a radio news bulletin accurately.
sla_exercise: What does a summary NOT contain?::Personal opinion or unnecessary details.||Give an expression to begin a summary.::Le texte parle de ... or En résumé, ....||List three question words used to summarise.::Qui, quoi, où (also quand, pourquoi).

sla_notes_intro: Pupils read varied texts and produce short summaries of the messages.
sla_notes_details: Steps: read the whole text, underline key sentences, identify the theme and the structure (introduction, development, conclusion), and reformulate. Reading types are skimming (survol), scanning (repérage) and detailed reading. Context clues and word families help with unknown words. The summary is written in the present tense in the third person and uses connectors to link ideas.
sla_notes_illustrations: Text on water conservation: after reading, a pupil writes: L'auteur explique qu'il faut économiser l'eau. Il propose de fermer le robinet et de recueillir l'eau de pluie.
sla_notes_daily_life: Reading and summarising newspapers, letters and school texts helps you study efficiently and share information.
sla_exercise: What is skimming?::Reading quickly to get the general idea.||In which tense is a summary usually written?::The present tense.||Name the three parts of a text's structure.::Introduction, development and conclusion.

sla_notes_intro: Pupils read longer texts aloud with expression, speed and assurance.
sla_notes_details: Expression depends on respecting punctuation, sense groups and intonation, and on pronouncing nasal vowels (an, en /ɑ̃/, on /ɔ̃/, in, ain /ɛ̃/, un /œ̃/), the French r, silent h (l'homme) and liaisons (vous avez /vuzave/). Pupils practise repeated reading, choral reading and recording themselves. Confidence grows by reading in front of a small group before the whole class.
sla_notes_illustrations: Pupils read a dialogue about a market: Combien coûtent les bananes ? Deux cents shillings le kilo. They pay attention to the nasal sounds in combien and cent.
sla_notes_daily_life: Reading confidently in front of others is useful for presentations, meetings and reading announcements.
sla_exercise: Which nasal vowel is in bon?::/ɔ̃/ (on).||What links vous and avez in vous avez?::A liaison /z/.||Give one way to improve fluency.::Reread the text several times or read aloud in groups.

sla_notes_intro: Pupils speak appropriately in familiar and less familiar situations, adjusting register.
sla_notes_details: Register: familiar with friends (Salut, ça va ?), formal with adults and officials (Bonjour Monsieur, comment allez-vous ?). Speech acts: presenting oneself, inviting (Tu veux venir ?), accepting and refusing (Avec plaisir, Désolé, je ne peux pas), apologising (Excusez-moi), giving an opinion (Je pense que, À mon avis) and thanking. Structures include the imperative for instructions (Ouvrez le livre), modals (pouvoir, vouloir, devoir) and the future proche. Body language and eye contact support communication.
sla_notes_illustrations: Role-play: a pupil invites a classmate to a birthday: Tu peux venir samedi à ma fête ? Response: Avec plaisir, à quelle heure ? Then the same invitation is made formally to a teacher.
sla_notes_daily_life: Choosing the right level of language lets you speak politely to elders and naturally to friends.
sla_exercise: Which pronoun is formal, tu or vous?::Vous.||Give a phrase to refuse an invitation politely.::Désolé, je ne peux pas.||Translate: In my opinion.::À mon avis.

sla_notes_intro: Pupils write short informative texts such as descriptions, invitations, notices and messages.
sla_notes_details: An invitation states who invites, what event, where, when (date and time) and how to reply (RSVP). A notice is short and gives event, place, date, time and contact. A description follows an order: general presentation, details, impression. Dates are written le 12 mai; times as huit heures trente or 8 h 30. Sentences use the present tense, il y a and adjectives with agreement.
sla_notes_illustrations: Invitation: Je t'invite à mon anniversaire le samedi 12 mai à 15 h, chez moi, rue du Marché. Réponds-moi avant jeudi. Amélie.
sla_notes_daily_life: Clear written information helps you announce events at school, in the community and at work.

sla_notes_intro: Paraphrasing means restating a heard message in different words while keeping the meaning. Pupils listen carefully and reformulate.
sla_notes_details: Techniques: replace words by synonyms (acheter becomes prendre), change the structure (active to passive, affirmative to negative with opposite: Il est grand becomes Il n'est pas petit), reorder clauses, and use reporting verbs. The paraphrase must keep all main information, be about the same length and not copy the original. Indirect speech shifts pronouns and time markers: aujourd'hui becomes ce jour-là, demain becomes le lendemain.
sla_notes_illustrations: Original: Le train part à huit heures. Paraphrase: Le départ du train est prévu à huit heures. Pupils listen to a short message, note the key points and paraphrase orally.
sla_notes_daily_life: Paraphrasing helps you explain instructions to someone who did not understand them the first time, or pass messages between speakers of different levels.
sla_exercise: What is a paraphrase?::A restatement of a message in different words with the same meaning.||Give a synonym for commencer.::Débuter.||Paraphrase: Il est petit.::Il n'est pas grand.

sla_notes_intro: Pupils read texts on different topics and present their content to the class.
sla_notes_details: Preparation: read the text twice, identify theme, main ideas and key vocabulary, and prepare notes rather than a full script. A presentation has an introduction (Je vais vous présenter ...), a development in two or three points (Premièrement, Deuxièmement, Enfin) and a conclusion (Pour conclure). Voice should be clear, speed moderate, and eye contact maintained. Visual aids like a poster can support the presentation. The audience may ask questions at the end.
sla_notes_illustrations: After reading a text about the Serengeti, a pupil presents: Aujourd'hui, je vais vous présenter le parc du Serengeti. D'abord, sa situation. Ensuite, ses animaux. Pour conclure, son importance pour le tourisme.
sla_notes_daily_life: Presenting information clearly is a useful skill in school projects, meetings and workplaces.
sla_exercise: Give the three parts of a presentation.::Introduction, development and conclusion.||Which phrase can begin a presentation?::Je vais vous présenter ...||Why should you keep eye contact?::To hold the audience's attention and show confidence.

sla_notes_intro: Pupils respond suitably to messages they hear, in words or in action.
sla_notes_details: Reactions depend on the function of the message: an invitation is accepted or refused; a request is granted or declined (Bien sûr, Je regrette); a piece of news brings congratulations (Félicitations !), sympathy (Je suis désolé) or surprise (Vraiment ?); an instruction leads to action. Politeness formulas (s'il vous plaît, merci, je vous en prie) are used. Vocabulary of agreement and disagreement: Je suis d'accord, Je ne suis pas d'accord, C'est vrai, Ce n'est pas vrai.
sla_notes_illustrations: Message: J'ai réussi mon examen ! Reaction: Félicitations ! Je suis très content pour toi. Message: Je ne peux pas venir. Reaction: Ce n'est pas grave, à la prochaine fois.
sla_notes_daily_life: Reacting properly to news and requests shows politeness and keeps conversations natural.
sla_exercise: React to: Je suis malade.::Je suis désolé, bon rétablissement !||Give an expression of agreement.::Je suis d'accord.||Answer: Merci beaucoup !::De rien or Je vous en prie.

sla_notes_intro: Pupils respond in writing to letters, notes, invitations and emails.
sla_notes_details: A written reply refers to the message received (Merci pour ta lettre du 3 mai), answers each question or request, adds news, and closes with a suitable formula. Reply to an invitation states acceptance or refusal and gives reasons: Je te remercie pour ton invitation, mais je ne pourrai pas venir car j'ai un examen. Tone is informal with friends and formal with officials. Check spelling, verb endings and agreement before sending.
sla_notes_illustrations: Message: Peux-tu venir à mon anniversaire samedi ? Reply: Merci pour ton invitation ! Je viendrai avec plaisir. À quelle heure commence la fête ?
sla_notes_daily_life: Replying properly to emails and messages is an important daily communication skill at school and at work.

sla_name: Characteristics of spoken and written French

sla_teaching_aids: Documents simples variés
sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D’ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ire À IVe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Spoken and written French differ in vocabulary, structure, sounds and marks. Pupils identify and use these characteristics, including lexicon, morphosyntax, accent, intonation, assimilation, elision, liaison, enchaînement, punctuation and orthographic signs.
sla_notes_details: Lexicon: spoken French uses colloquial words (le boulot, la bagnole), written French uses standard words (le travail, la voiture). Morphosyntax: spoken language may drop ne in the negative (Je sais pas), while writing keeps ne ... pas; questions by intonation in speech, by inversion in writing. Sounds: elision removes a vowel before a vowel (l'école, j'aime), liaison links a final consonant to a vowel (des amis), enchaînement pronounces a final consonant with the next vowel (il aime /i-lɛm/). Written French adds accents, cedilla, silent endings for agreement (les petites filles), punctuation and capital letters. The oral code uses intonation, rhythm and gesture; the written code uses spelling and layout.
sla_notes_illustrations: Speech: Je sais pas, c'est où le marché ? Writing: Je ne sais pas où se trouve le marché. Pupils compare the two and note which features change.
sla_notes_daily_life: Knowing the difference lets you write formally in reports and letters and speak naturally in conversation.
sla_exercise: What is elision? Give an example.::Dropping a final vowel before a vowel sound, as in l'école.||Rewrite formally: Je sais pas.::Je ne sais pas.||Which phenomenon links the s in des amis?::Liaison.

sla_notes_intro: Pupils choose the right form of French for the situation, including applying the features studied to express themselves.
sla_notes_details: Context determines register: informal (conversation among friends, text messages), neutral (school), formal (official letters, interviews). In formal contexts use vous, full negation, complete sentences, polite conditional (Je voudrais, Pourriez-vous) and formulas such as Veuillez agréer ... In informal contexts contractions and colloquial terms are acceptable. In writing, check punctuation, accent, orthographic signs and agreement; in speaking, control accent, intonation, liaison and elision.
sla_notes_illustrations: Formal: Pourriez-vous me dire où se trouve la poste ? Informal: Tu sais où est la poste ? Pupils take a situation card (interview, chat with a friend) and choose the right register.
sla_notes_daily_life: Adapting language to the audience is essential in job interviews, meetings and social conversations.
sla_exercise: Which is formal: Tu sais or Pourriez-vous?::Pourriez-vous.||Give a formal closing formula for a letter.::Veuillez agréer, Monsieur, mes salutations distinguées.||Why change register?::To suit the audience and situation.

sla_notes_intro: Pupils participate in dialogues in familiar and less familiar or formal contexts.
sla_notes_details: A conversation has an opening (Bonjour, Salut), an exchange with questions and answers, turn-taking, and a closing (Au revoir, À bientôt). To keep it going, use reactions (Ah bon ?, C'est intéressant), requests for repetition (Pouvez-vous répéter, s'il vous plaît ?) and clarification (Qu'est-ce que vous voulez dire ?). Familiar topics: hobbies, school, family; formal: an interview, a shop, a bank. Use appropriate vocabulary and register.
sla_notes_illustrations: Dialogue in a shop: Bonjour Madame, je voudrais un cahier. Voilà. Combien coûte-t-il ? Cinq cents shillings. Merci, au revoir.
sla_notes_daily_life: Taking part in conversations gives you confidence when dealing with French speakers in tourism, trade or study.
sla_exercise: Ask someone to repeat.::Pouvez-vous répéter, s'il vous plaît ?||Give a closing expression.::Au revoir or À bientôt.||Translate: How much does it cost?::Combien ça coûte ?

sla_notes_intro: Pupils write coherent texts on different subjects such as descriptions, narrations and reports.
sla_notes_details: Process: plan (brainstorm, order ideas), draft, revise, edit. Structure: introduction, development, conclusion. Narration uses passé composé and imparfait: Il faisait beau quand nous sommes partis. Description uses the present and adjectives. Connectors: d'abord, puis, mais, cependant, parce que, donc, finalement. Length is about 100 to 150 words. Vocabulary is chosen to fit the topic; spelling and agreement are checked.
sla_notes_illustrations: Topic: Ma journée à l'école. Pupil: Le matin, j'arrive à l'école à sept heures. Je suis en classe jusqu'à midi. L'après-midi, je joue au football avec mes amis.
sla_notes_daily_life: Writing skill is needed for school assignments, blogs, reports and messages.
sla_exercise: What are the four stages of the writing process?::Plan, draft, revise and edit.||Give a connector expressing contrast.::Mais or cependant.||Which tense describes past ongoing conditions?::The imparfait.

sla_notes_intro: Pupils learn the layout and style of a formal letter used for requests, applications and complaints.
sla_notes_details: Layout: sender's name and address at top left; recipient's name and address at right; place and date; subject line (Objet : demande de stage); salutation (Monsieur, Madame, Monsieur le Directeur); body in three parts (introduction stating purpose, development with details, conclusion with request or thanks); closing formula (Veuillez agréer, Monsieur, l'expression de mes salutations distinguées); signature. Style is polite and impersonal, using vous, the conditional (je souhaiterais) and no abbreviations or slang. Paragraphs are clear and short.
sla_notes_illustrations: Objet : demande d'inscription. Monsieur le Directeur, Je souhaiterais m'inscrire en cours de français. Je vous remercie de bien vouloir me répondre. Veuillez agréer, Monsieur le Directeur, mes salutations distinguées. Asha Juma.
sla_notes_daily_life: Formal letters are used for job applications, school admissions and official requests.
sla_exercise: What is the Objet line?::The subject line stating the purpose of the letter.||Which pronoun is used in formal letters?::Vous.||Give a French formal closing formula.::Veuillez agréer, Monsieur, mes salutations distinguées.

sla_notes_intro: Pupils listen to a message and express and justify their point of view.
sla_notes_details: Expressing opinion: Je pense que, Je crois que, À mon avis, Selon moi, Pour moi. Agreement: Je suis d'accord avec ... Disagreement: Je ne suis pas d'accord parce que .... Justification uses parce que, car, puisque, en effet, par exemple. Structure: state the opinion, give reasons, illustrate with an example, conclude. Respect for others' views is essential, using formulas like Je comprends votre point de vue, mais ....
sla_notes_illustrations: After hearing a report on mobile phones in schools: À mon avis, les téléphones sont utiles parce qu'on peut chercher des informations, mais ils distraient les élèves en classe.
sla_notes_daily_life: Giving reasoned opinions is useful in discussions, debates and decisions at home and in the community.

sla_notes_intro: Pupils read narratives and folktales and understand their plot, characters and message.
sla_notes_details: Narrative elements: characters (personnages), setting (lieu et temps), plot in stages (situation initiale, élément déclencheur, péripéties, dénouement, situation finale) and moral. Tenses: passé simple in literary tales (Il était une fois ..., le lion se leva), imparfait for description, passé composé in oral stories. Comprehension questions ask who, where, what happened, why and what lesson is taught. Pupils identify emotions and infer meaning from context.
sla_notes_illustrations: Tale: Il était une fois un lièvre rusé qui vivait dans la savane. Pupils identify the character (le lièvre), the setting (la savane) and later the moral: la ruse ne remplace pas l'honnêteté.
sla_notes_daily_life: Stories carry cultural values and moral lessons and develop reading pleasure and imagination.
sla_exercise: Which phrase traditionally opens a tale?::Il était une fois ...||Name the stages of a plot.::Initial situation, triggering event, developments, resolution and final situation.||What is the moral of a story?::The lesson it teaches.

sla_notes_intro: Pupils tell events orally in a logical sequence.
sla_notes_details: Narration uses the passé composé for actions and the imparfait for background: Il pleuvait quand je suis sorti. Time markers order events: d'abord, puis, ensuite, après, pendant que, soudain, enfin, hier, la semaine dernière. Agreement of the past participle with être (Elle est partie) and with a preceding direct object (la lettre que j'ai écrite) is respected. A story has a beginning, middle and end and uses voice and gesture to hold attention.
sla_notes_illustrations: Pupil tells: Hier, je suis allé au marché. Soudain, il a commencé à pleuvoir. Alors, je me suis abrité sous un arbre. Enfin, la pluie a cessé et je suis rentré.
sla_notes_daily_life: Narrating events helps you report incidents, tell family stories and share experiences.
sla_exercise: Which tense expresses background description in the past?::The imparfait.||Give two time markers.::D'abord and ensuite (also puis, enfin).||Put in the passé composé: Elle part.::Elle est partie.

sla_notes_intro: Pupils discuss and debate topics such as environment, health and technology, respecting rules of debate.
sla_notes_details: Debate roles: moderator (modérateur), speakers for and against, audience. Language: Je voudrais ajouter que, Certes ..., mais ..., D'une part ... d'autre part, En revanche, Par conséquent. Arguments require a claim, evidence and an example. Rules: raise hand, do not interrupt, listen, respect time, stay on topic. Debate topics: Les téléphones portables à l'école, La protection de l'environnement. The debate ends with a conclusion by each side.
sla_notes_illustrations: Motion: Il faut interdire les sacs en plastique. For: D'une part, ils polluent les rivières. Against: Certes, mais ils sont pratiques pour les petits commerçants.
sla_notes_daily_life: Debating develops critical thinking, respect for others and public speaking used in civic life.
sla_exercise: Who guides a debate?::The moderator.||Give a phrase to introduce contrast.::Certes ... mais ... or en revanche.||Name one rule of debating.::Do not interrupt others.

sla_notes_intro: Pupils compose texts of different types such as narrative, descriptive, argumentative, informative and dialogue.
sla_notes_details: Text types have distinct features: narrative (chronology, past tenses), descriptive (present or imparfait, adjectives, comparisons), argumentative (thesis, arguments, connectors of cause and consequence), informative (facts, headings), dialogue (tirets and guillemets). Composition includes title, paragraphs, connectors and a conclusion, at about 150 to 200 words. Editing verifies verb forms, agreement, spelling, punctuation and vocabulary variety.
sla_notes_illustrations: Argumentative paragraph: Je pense que l'école doit enseigner l'informatique. Premièrement, elle prépare aux métiers modernes. Deuxièmement, elle facilite la recherche. En conclusion, c'est indispensable.
sla_notes_daily_life: Composing different texts prepares you for writing reports, articles, applications and stories.
sla_exercise: Name two text types.::Narrative and descriptive (also argumentative).||What tense do informative texts mostly use?::The present.||Give a conclusion connector.::Enfin or en conclusion.

learning_activity_name: Traduire des documents simples
sla_assessment_criteria: Capacité de traduire des documents correctement.
sla_teaching_aids: Textes simples|Textes authentiques. Semi authentiques pour faire la traduction
sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D’ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ire À IVe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Pupils translate short simple texts between French, English and Kiswahili with attention to meaning.
sla_notes_details: Translation transfers meaning, not word for word. Steps: read the whole text, identify the type and purpose, translate sentence by sentence keeping the message, choose equivalent expressions, and reread for naturalness. Beware of false friends such as actuellement meaning currently, not actually; librairie meaning bookshop, not library; and of idioms: Il pleut des cordes means it is raining heavily. Word order differs: une voiture rouge is a red car. Use a dictionary to check terms and keep the register.
sla_notes_illustrations: Translate: The library opens at nine. La bibliothèque ouvre à neuf heures. Translate: Il fait froid aujourd'hui. It is cold today. Pupils then translate a notice and compare in pairs.
sla_notes_daily_life: Translation is useful for tourism, business documents, signs and communication between languages.
sla_exercise: What does actuellement mean?::Currently, at present.||Translate: It is cold today.::Il fait froid aujourd'hui.||Why is word-for-word translation risky?::Idioms and structures differ, so the meaning may be lost.

learning_activity_name: Interpréter des conversations simples
sla_assessment_criteria: Capacité d’interpréter des conversations simples Correctement.
sla_teaching_aids: Vidéos enregistré d’interpréter
sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D’ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ire À IVe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Interpreting is the oral transfer of a spoken message from one language to another. Pupils practise with short conversations.
sla_notes_details: Types: consecutive (interpreter speaks after the speaker pauses) and simultaneous. At this level, consecutive interpreting with note-taking is used. Skills: active listening, memorising key ideas, using symbols or key words in notes, speaking clearly in the first person (Je voudrais ... not Il dit qu'il voudrait ...), staying neutral and confidential. Interpreters clarify only when necessary and keep the register of the speaker.
sla_notes_illustrations: A tourist says: Bonjour, où est le marché ? The pupil interprets in English: Hello, where is the market? and interprets the guide's reply into French: Le marché est à côté de la gare.
sla_notes_daily_life: Interpreting helps guides, hotel staff and traders communicate with visitors.
sla_exercise: What is consecutive interpreting?::Interpreting after the speaker pauses.||Should the interpreter give personal opinions?::No, the interpreter stays neutral.||Which person does an interpreter use?::The first person, as the speaker does.

sla_references: TET(2023), PROGRAMME D’ENSEIGNEMENT DU FRANÇAIS LANGUE ÉTRANGÈRE, ENSEIGNEMENT SECONDAIRE DE Ire À IVe ANNÉE, TET, DAR ES SALAAM
sla_notes_intro: Editing means checking and correcting a text to improve accuracy, clarity and style.
sla_notes_details: Editing checklist: spelling and accents; verb tense and conjugation; subject-verb agreement; adjective and participle agreement; gender of nouns; punctuation and capitalisation; repetition and word choice; logical order and connectors. Proofreading marks include underline, insertion and deletion. Read the text aloud to detect errors, then compare with a dictionary and grammar reference. Peer editing helps by giving feedback.
sla_notes_illustrations: Text: Les enfant joue dans le jardin. Corrected: Les enfants jouent dans le jardin. Pupils exchange notebooks and correct three errors in each other's texts.
sla_notes_daily_life: Editing improves reports, letters and applications so that they are clear and error-free.
sla_exercise: Correct: Elle sont partie.::Elles sont parties.||Give one item on an editing checklist.::Spelling, agreement, punctuation, tense (any one).||Why read aloud when editing?::It helps you detect errors and awkward sentences.
